question:
Which of the following statements is NOT correct regarding sound?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Sound can travel through vacuum.
In human beings, the vibration of vocal cords produce sound.
Unpleasant sounds are called noise.
Frequency is expressed in hertz.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Sound can travel through vacuum.

Explanation:
Sound is a mechanical wave that requires a medium (solid, liquid, or gas) to propagate. In a vacuum, there is no medium, so sound cannot travel through it. This is why sound cannot be heard in space. The other options are correct: in human beings, the vibration of vocal cords produces sound, unpleasant sounds are called noise, and frequency is expressed in hertz (Hz).

Extra Facts:
Sound waves are longitudinal waves, where the particles of the medium vibrate in the same direction as the wave. The speed of sound depends on the density and elasticity of the medium. Sound travels fastest in solids because the particles are closer together and can vibrate more quickly. Sound is used in medicine (ultrasound), communication, and entertainment (music).

☛ What type of waves are sound waves? → Longitudinal waves
☛ What frequency range can the human ear hear? → 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz
☛ In what unit is sound intensity measured? → Decibel (dB)
☛ What is the frequency of ultrasonic sound? → Above 20,000 Hz
question_hi:
ध्वनि के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कथन सही नहीं है?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options_hi: ध्वनि निर्वात में संचारित हो सकती है।
मानव वाक् तंतुओं के कंपन द्वारा ध्वनि उत्पन्न करते हैं।
अप्रिय ध्वनियाँ शोर कहलाती हैं।
आवृत्ति को हर्ट्ज (Hz) में व्यक्त करते हैं।
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है ध्वनि निर्वात में संचारित हो सकती है।

Explanation:
ध्वनि एक यांत्रिक तरंग है जिसे संचारित होने के लिए एक माध्यम (ठोस, द्रव या गैस) की आवश्यकता होती है। निर्वात में कोई माध्यम नहीं होता है, इसलिए ध्वनि निर्वात में संचारित नहीं हो सकती है। यही कारण है कि अंतरिक्ष में ध्वनि नहीं सुनी जा सकती है। अन्य विकल्प सही हैं: मानव वाक् तंतुओं के कंपन से ध्वनि उत्पन्न होती है, अप्रिय ध्वनियों को शोर कहा जाता है, और आवृत्ति को हर्ट्ज (Hz) में मापा जाता है।

Extra Facts:
ध्वनि तरंगें अनुदैर्ध्य तरंगें होती हैं, जिसमें माध्यम के कण तरंग की दिशा में ही कंपन करते हैं। ध्वनि की गति माध्यम के घनत्व और लोच पर निर्भर करती है। ठोस में ध्वनि की गति सबसे अधिक होती है, क्योंकि इसमें कणों के बीच की दूरी कम होती है और वे तेजी से कंपन कर सकते हैं। ध्वनि का उपयोग चिकित्सा (अल्ट्रासाउंड), संचार और मनोरंजन (संगीत) में किया जाता है।

question:
Among the given options, which one causes an echo?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: When sound is reflected
When sound waves travel through a solid medium
When sound waves travel through a liquid medium
When sound waves travel through a vacuum
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is When sound is reflected

Explanation:
An echo is produced when sound waves reflect off a large and hard surface (e.g., mountains, walls, or buildings) and return to the listener. This phenomenon is based on the principle of reflection. For an echo to be heard distinctly, the minimum distance between the reflecting surface and the sound source must be 17.2 meters (at 20°C) because the human ear cannot distinguish between sounds separated by less than 0.1 seconds. If the distance is shorter, the original sound and its echo merge, making the echo indistinguishable.

Extra Facts:
1. Echo is used in SONAR (Sound Navigation and Ranging) to measure ocean depths and detect submarines.
2. The speed of sound depends on the medium's density: solid > liquid > gas. Sound cannot travel in a vacuum as it is a mechanical wave requiring a medium.
3. Reverberation occurs when sound reflects multiple times, prolonging the sound, as in halls or caves.

☛ What type of waves are sound waves? → Longitudinal waves
question_hi:
दिए गए विकल्पों में से कौन-सा विकल्प प्रतिध्वनि उत्पन्न करता है?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options_hi: जब ध्वनि परावर्तित होती है
जब ध्वनि तरंगें किसी ठोस माध्यम से होकर गुजरती हैं
जब ध्वनि तरंगें किसी तरल माध्यम से होकर गुजरती हैं
जब ध्वनि तरंगें निर्वात से होकर गुजरती हैं
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है जब ध्वनि परावर्तित होती है

Explanation:
प्रतिध्वनि (Echo) तब उत्पन्न होती है जब ध्वनि तरंगें किसी बड़े और कठोर सतह (जैसे पहाड़, दीवार, या इमारत) से टकराकर वापस लौटती हैं। यह परावर्तन (Reflection) के सिद्धांत पर काम करता है। प्रतिध्वनि सुनने के लिए, परावर्तक सतह और ध्वनि स्रोत के बीच न्यूनतम दूरी 17.2 मीटर होनी चाहिए (20°C तापमान पर), क्योंकि मानव कान 0.1 सेकंड से कम समय के अंतराल को अलग नहीं कर सकता। यदि दूरी कम होगी, तो ध्वनि और उसकी प्रतिध्वनि एक साथ सुनाई देंगी, जिससे प्रतिध्वनि स्पष्ट नहीं होगी।

Extra Facts:
1. प्रतिध्वनि का उपयोग सोनार (SONAR) में किया जाता है, जो समुद्र की गहराई मापने और पनडुब्बियों का पता लगाने में मदद करता है।
2. ध्वनि की गति माध्यम के घनत्व पर निर्भर करती है: ठोस > तरल > गैस। निर्वात में ध्वनि नहीं चल सकती क्योंकि यह एक यांत्रिक तरंग है जिसे संचरण के लिए माध्यम की आवश्यकता होती है।
3. 'रेवरबरेशन' (Reverberation) वह घटना है जब ध्वनि कई बार परावर्तित होती है और ध्वनि लंबे समय तक सुनाई देती है, जैसे हॉल या गुफा में।

question:
We hear others speaking to us from adjacent rooms due to _______ of sound waves.

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: echo
reflection
diffraction
refraction
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is diffraction

Explanation:
The diffraction of sound waves is the phenomenon where waves bend around the edges of obstacles or openings and spread into the region behind them. When we hear people speaking from adjacent rooms, it's because sound waves diffract around doorways or wall edges. Diffraction allows sound waves to pass through small openings and reach us. This phenomenon is more pronounced when the wavelength is comparable to or larger than the size of the obstacle or opening.

Extra Facts:
Sound wave diffraction can be observed in many everyday situations, such as water waves bending around rocks. This phenomenon occurs not only with sound waves but also with light waves, though light's much smaller wavelength makes its diffraction less noticeable. Sound diffraction is what enables us to hear distant sounds even when there are obstacles in the direct path. The ability of sound to diffract is crucial for hearing in complex environments and is the reason we can hear around corners.

☛ What is the speed of sound in air? → 343 m/s (at 20°C)
☛ What is the unit for measuring noise? → Decibel (dB)
☛ What principle does sonar technology work on? → Reflection of sound waves

Explanation:
ध्वनि तरंगों का विवर्तन (Diffraction) वह घटना है जिसमें तरंगें किसी अवरोध या छिद्र के किनारों से मुड़कर उसके पीछे के क्षेत्र में फैल जाती हैं। जब हम बगल के कमरों से आवाज़ सुनते हैं, तो यह ध्वनि तरंगों के दरवाज़े या दीवारों के किनारों से विवर्तित होने के कारण होता है। विवर्तन के कारण ध्वनि तरंगें छोटे-छोटे रास्तों से भी गुजरकर हम तक पहुँचती हैं। यह घटना तब अधिक स्पष्ट होती है जब तरंगदैर्ध्य अवरोध या छिद्र के आकार के समान या बड़ा होता है।

Extra Facts:
ध्वनि तरंगों का विवर्तन रोज़मर्रा की ज़िंदगी में कई जगह देखा जा सकता है, जैसे कि पानी की लहरों का पत्थरों के पीछे मुड़ना। यह घटना केवल ध्वनि तरंगों में ही नहीं, बल्कि प्रकाश तरंगों में भी देखी जा सकती है, लेकिन प्रकाश का तरंगदैर्ध्य बहुत छोटा होने के कारण इसका विवर्तन कम स्पष्ट होता है। ध्वनि तरंगों का विवर्तन ही हमें दूर से आने वाली आवाज़ों को सुनने में सक्षम बनाता है, भले ही सीधी रेखा में कोई अवरोध हो।

question:
The way the brain interprets the frequency of an emitted sound is called the ________.

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: amplitude
sound
pitch
wave
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is pitch

Explanation:
The interpretation of the frequency of a sound wave by the brain is called 'pitch'. Frequency refers to the number of vibrations per second of a sound wave, measured in Hertz (Hz). High-frequency sounds (e.g., a bird's chirp) are perceived as high-pitched, while low-frequency sounds (e.g., a bass drum) are perceived as low-pitched. The brain determines pitch by analyzing the frequency of sound waves received by the ear. This process is a crucial function of the auditory system.

Extra Facts:
Other important properties of sound waves include 'amplitude', which determines the loudness of a sound. The greater the amplitude, the louder the sound. Sound waves are longitudinal waves, created by the compression and rarefaction of particles in a medium (e.g., air, water). Humans can hear sounds in the frequency range of 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz. Frequencies above this range are called ultrasonic, and those below are called infrasonic.

question_hi:

ध्वनि

solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है पिच

Explanation:
ध्वनि की आवृत्ति (frequency) का मस्तिष्क द्वारा व्याख्या किए जाने को 'पिच' कहा जाता है। आवृत्ति ध्वनि तरंगों के प्रति सेकंड कंपन की संख्या होती है, जिसे हर्ट्ज़ (Hz) में मापा जाता है। उच्च आवृत्ति वाली ध्वनियों (जैसे चिड़िया की चहचहाहट) को हम उच्च पिच के रूप में सुनते हैं, जबकि निम्न आवृत्ति वाली ध्वनियों (जैसे बास ड्रम) को निम्न पिच के रूप में सुनते हैं। मस्तिष्क कान द्वारा प्राप्त ध्वनि तरंगों की आवृत्ति की व्याख्या करके पिच का निर्धारण करता है। यह प्रक्रिया श्रवण प्रणाली (auditory system) का एक महत्वपूर्ण कार्य है।

Extra Facts:
ध्वनि तरंगों के अन्य महत्वपूर्ण गुणों में 'आयाम' (amplitude) शामिल है, जो ध्वनि की तीव्रता (loudness) को निर्धारित करता है। आयाम जितना अधिक होगा, ध्वनि उतनी ही तेज सुनाई देगी। ध्वनि तरंगें अनुदैर्ध्य तरंगें (longitudinal waves) होती हैं, जो माध्यम (जैसे हवा, पानी) के कणों के संपीडन और विरलन से बनती हैं। मनुष्य 20 Hz से 20,000 Hz तक की आवृत्तियों वाली ध्वनियों को सुन सकता है। इस सीमा से ऊपर की ध्वनियों को अल्ट्रासोनिक (ultrasonic) और नीचे की ध्वनियों को इन्फ्रासोनिक (infrasonic) कहा जाता है।

question:
For humans, the audible waves are those that:

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options:
have the frequency below 20 Hz

have the frequency above 2000 Hz

have the frequency range between 200 Hz to 2000 Hz

have the frequency range between 20 Hz to 20000 Hz
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is have the frequency range between 20 Hz to 20000 Hz

Explanation:
For humans, audible waves are sound waves with frequencies between 20 Hz and 20,000 Hz (20 kHz). This is known as the audible range. Sound waves are mechanical waves that propagate through a medium (such as air or water). Waves with frequencies below 20 Hz are called infrasonic waves, while those with frequencies above 20,000 Hz are called ultrasonic waves. The human ear cannot detect these two types of waves. The audible range decreases with age, particularly the ability to hear higher frequencies.

Extra Facts:
The speed of sound waves depends on the density and elasticity of the medium. In air, the speed of sound is approximately 343 m/s (at 20°C). Ultrasonic waves are used in medical imaging (ultrasound), sonar, and industrial applications. Infrasonic waves are generated by natural phenomena such as earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, and some large animals (elephants, whales).

Important one-liners for upcoming exams
☛ What type of waves are sound waves? → Mechanical waves
☛ What is the speed of sound in air? → 343 m/s (at 20°C)
☛ What is the frequency range of infrasonic waves? → Below 20 Hz
☛ What is the frequency range of ultrasonic waves? → Above 20,000 Hz
☛ How does the audible range change with age in humans? → Decreases

मनुष्यों के लिए श्रव्य तरंगें वे ध्वनि तरंगें हैं जिनकी आवृत्ति 20 Hz से 20,000 Hz (20 kHz) के बीच होती है। यह श्रव्य परास (audible range) कहलाता है। ध्वनि तरंगें यांत्रिक तरंगें होती हैं जो किसी माध्यम (जैसे हवा, पानी) में संचरित होती हैं। 20 Hz से कम आवृत्ति वाली तरंगों को अवश्रव्य तरंगें (infrasonic waves) कहते हैं, जबकि 20,000 Hz से अधिक आवृत्ति वाली तरंगों को पराश्रव्य तरंगें (ultrasonic waves) कहते हैं। मनुष्य का कान इन दोनों प्रकार की तरंगों को नहीं सुन सकता। श्रव्य परास उम्र के साथ घटता है, विशेषकर उच्च आवृत्तियों की सुनने की क्षमता।

Extra Facts:
ध्वनि तरंगों की गति माध्यम के घनत्व और लोच पर निर्भर करती है। हवा में ध्वनि की गति लगभग 343 m/s (20°C पर) होती है। पराश्रव्य तरंगों का उपयोग चिकित्सा इमेजिंग (अल्ट्रासाउंड), सोनार, और औद्योगिक अनुप्रयोगों में किया जाता है। अवश्रव्य तरंगें प्राकृतिक घटनाओं जैसे भूकंप, ज्वालामुखी विस्फोट और कुछ बड़े जानवरों (हाथी, व्हेल) द्वारा उत्पन्न की जाती हैं।

question:
The number of oscillations per second is called_______.

[SSC GD 2024]
options: pitch
frequency
Hutters
dimension
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is frequency

Explanation:
Frequency refers to the number of oscillations per second of a periodic phenomenon. It is measured in Hertz (Hz). For example, if an object completes 50 oscillations in 1 second, its frequency is 50 Hz. The formula for frequency is:
f = 1/T, where f is frequency and T is the time period.
Frequency is crucial in studying sound, light, and other waves. It relates to the pitch of sound, but pitch is the perceived 'highness' or 'lowness', whereas frequency is a scientific measurement.

Extra Facts:
1. The human ear can hear sound frequencies between 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz.
2. Radio waves have frequencies ranging from kHz to GHz.
3. The unit Hertz (Hz) is named after German physicist Heinrich Hertz, who studied electromagnetic waves.
4. Ultrasound (>20 kHz) and infrasound (<20 Hz) are inaudible to humans.

f = 1/T, जहाँ f आवृत्ति है और T आवर्तकाल (Time period) है।
आवृत्ति ध्वनि, प्रकाश और अन्य तरंगों के अध्ययन में महत्वपूर्ण है। यह ध्वनि के तारत्व (Pitch) से संबंधित है, लेकिन तारत्व ध्वनि की 'ऊँचाई' का अनुभव है, जबकि आवृत्ति एक वैज्ञानिक माप है।

question:
The device that uses ultrasonic waves to measure the distance, direction and speed of underwater objects is called:

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: SONAR
RADAR
CRO
MASER
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is SONAR

Explanation:
SONAR (Sound Navigation And Ranging) is a device that uses ultrasonic waves to measure the distance, direction, and speed of underwater objects. This technology works on the principle of echo (sound reflection). When the ultrasonic waves emitted by SONAR hit an object, they reflect back. Based on this echo, the distance and direction of the object are calculated. This technique is widely used in naval operations, fishing, and marine research.

Extra Facts:
SONAR is of two types: Active SONAR and Passive SONAR. Active SONAR emits sound waves and records the echo, while Passive SONAR only listens to the sound waves present in the environment. RADAR (Radio Detection And Ranging) works similarly but uses radio waves and is primarily used for detecting aerial and ground objects.

☛ Which technology is used in submarines? → SONAR

question:
Through which of the following mediums can sound NOT travel?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Steel
Vacuum
Air
Milk
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Vacuum

Explanation:
Sound is a mechanical wave that requires a medium (solid, liquid, or gas) to travel. Sound waves propagate through the vibration of particles. A vacuum contains no particles, so sound cannot travel through it. Steel (solid), air (gas), and milk (liquid) are all mediums through which sound waves can travel. Sound travels fastest in solids because the particles are closely packed and bonds are stronger.

Extra Facts:
The speed of sound varies in different mediums. It is highest in solids (about 5130 m/s in iron), moderate in liquids (about 1482 m/s in water), and lowest in gases (about 343 m/s in air). Light can travel through a vacuum because it is an electromagnetic wave and does not require a medium. Sound waves are called 'longitudinal waves' because particles vibrate parallel to the direction of wave propagation.

☛ In which medium does sound travel fastest? → Solid
☛ In which medium can light NOT travel? → Darkness (incorrect, light can travel in vacuum)
☛ What is the nature of sound waves? → Longitudinal waves
☛ What is the speed of sound in air? → 343 m/s (at 20°C)

question:
Which of the following units is used to measure the intensity of sound?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Decibel
Pascal
Curie
Joule
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Decibel

Explanation:
The decibel (dB) is the unit used to measure the intensity of sound. It is a logarithmic unit that expresses the Sound Pressure Level (SPL), taking into account the sensitivity of the human ear. The decibel scale defines 0 dB as the threshold of human hearing, while sounds above 120 dB can cause pain.

Pascal is the unit of pressure, Curie measures radioactivity, and Joule is the unit of energy. None of these are used to measure sound intensity.

Extra Facts:
1. Sound waves are mechanical waves that require a medium (air, water, solids) for propagation.
2. The human ear can hear sounds between 20 Hz and 20,000 Hz.
3. Bel (B) is another unit for sound intensity, where 1 Bel = 10 decibels.
4. Excessive noise pollution (above 85 dB) can cause permanent hearing damage.

question:
The repeated reflection that results in the persistence of sound is called:

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: reverberation
echo
sonic boom
reflection
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is reverberation

Explanation:
The repeated reflection of sound that results in the persistence of sound is called reverberation. This occurs when sound waves reflect multiple times in an enclosed space (like a hall or room), creating a continuous sound effect. The reverberation time exceeds 0.1 seconds, making it difficult to distinguish between the original and reflected sound. This phenomenon is crucial in music halls and theaters, where it enhances sound quality.

Extra Facts:
The key difference between echo and reverberation is time. An echo is heard distinctly when the reflected sound arrives after 0.1 seconds, while reverberation involves immediate reflections. A sonic boom is a different phenomenon caused by objects traveling faster than the speed of sound. The principle of sound reflection is used in technologies like SONAR and echocardiography.

question:
Among the given options, which one causes an echo ?

[SSC MTS 2023]
options: When sound is reflected
When sound waves travel through a solid medium
When sound waves travel through a liquid medium
When sound waves travel through a vacuum
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is When sound is reflected

Explanation:
An echo is produced when sound waves reflect off a large and hard surface (e.g., mountains, walls, or buildings) and return to the listener. For an echo to be heard, the reflecting surface must be at least 17 meters away from the sound source to ensure a minimum time gap of 0.1 seconds between the original and reflected sound (required for human ears to distinguish them). This phenomenon is based on the law of reflection, where the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection.

Extra Facts:
• Echoes are used in SONAR technology to measure ocean depths or detect submarines.
• Bats and dolphins use echolocation to navigate in darkness.
• If the reflecting surface is too close (e.g., a room's wall), reverberation occurs instead of a distinct echo.

question:
How long will a sound wave take to travel 1.5 km, which has a frequency of 5 kHz and wavelength of 6 cm?

[SSC CGL 2024]
options: 2.5 seconds
50 seconds
5 seconds
25 seconds
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 5 seconds

Explanation:
The speed (v) of a sound wave can be calculated using the formula v = f × λ, where f is frequency (5 kHz = 5000 Hz) and λ is wavelength (6 cm = 0.06 m).
Thus, v = 5000 × 0.06 = 300 m/s
Now, time (t) taken to cover 1.5 km (1500 m) = distance / speed = 1500 / 300 = 5 seconds

Extra Facts:
Sound waves are mechanical waves that require a medium for propagation. The speed of sound in air is approximately 343 m/s (at 20°C), but it depends on temperature, humidity, and medium density. Sound travels faster in water (~1482 m/s) and steel (~5960 m/s). The audible frequency range for humans is 20 Hz to 20 kHz.

question:
The speed of sound _____________ as it passes from solid to gaseous medium.

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Fluctuates
Increases
Does not change
Decreases
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Decreases

Explanation:
The speed of sound depends on the density and elasticity of the medium. In solids, molecules are closely packed and highly elastic, allowing sound waves to travel faster. In contrast, gaseous mediums have molecules that are far apart and less elastic, resulting in slower sound propagation. Therefore, when sound passes from a solid to a gaseous medium, its speed decreases. This principle is crucial for understanding sound transmission and comparing sound speeds in different media.

Extra Facts:
The speed of sound varies in different media. For example, in air, it is approximately 343 m/s (at 20°C), in water 1482 m/s, and in steel about 5960 m/s. The speed of sound also depends on temperature, pressure, and the density of the medium. This information is vital in seismic wave studies and sonar technology.

question:
In which unit, noise pollution is measured ?

[SSC GD 2024]
options: Centimeter
Ohm

Hertz
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Decibel

Explanation:
Noise pollution is measured in Decibel (dB). It is a logarithmic unit used to measure the intensity of sound or noise level. On the decibel scale, 0 dB represents the minimum threshold of human hearing, while sounds above 120 dB can cause pain. This unit is used for measuring noise pollution because it effectively represents the human ear's sensitivity to sound.

Extra Facts:
Some important facts about noise pollution:
- 30-60 dB level represents normal conversation or quiet environment.
- Sounds above 85 dB can cause hearing damage if exposed for prolonged periods.
- Sounds above 140 dB can immediately rupture eardrums.
- The decibel scale was invented by scientists at Bell Telephone Laboratories.

question:
Sonar is a device that uses ultrasonic waves to measure the distance, direction and speed of objects_______.

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: on land
in air
in space
underwater
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is underwater

Explanation:
Sonar (Sound Navigation and Ranging) is a technology that uses ultrasonic waves (sound waves with frequency >20 kHz) to detect the distance, direction, and speed of objects underwater. It works on the principle of echo, where sound waves reflect back after hitting an object, and the distance is calculated based on the time delay. Sonar is primarily used in submarines, marine navigation, fishing, and oceanographic research.

Extra Facts:
1. There are two types of sonar: Active Sonar (emits signals and measures echoes) and Passive Sonar (only listens to sounds, does not emit signals).
2. Dolphins and bats naturally use a similar technique called echolocation.
3. Sonar technology was invented by Paul Langevin in 1915.

सोनार (SONAR - Sound Navigation and Ranging) एक ऐसी तकनीक है जो अल्ट्रासोनिक तरंगों (20 kHz से अधिक आवृत्ति वाली ध्वनि तरंगें) का उपयोग करके जल के नीचे वस्तुओं की दूरी, दिशा और गति का पता लगाती है। यह तकनीक प्रतिध्वनि (Echo) के सिद्धांत पर काम करती है, जहाँ ध्वनि तरंगें वस्तु से टकराकर वापस लौटती हैं और समय अंतराल के आधार पर दूरी की गणना की जाती है। सोनार का उपयोग मुख्य रूप से पनडुब्बियों, समुद्री नेविगेशन, मछली पकड़ने और समुद्री अनुसंधान में किया जाता है।

question:
The ultrasonic waves sent inside a metal block to find out an invisible crack or a hole in it is found using-

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Absorber
Reflector
Wave producer
Detectors to detect the transmitted waves
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Detectors to detect the transmitted waves

Explanation:
Ultrasonic waves are used to detect invisible cracks or holes in metal blocks through a technique known as Ultrasonic Testing (UT). In this method, ultrasonic waves (sound waves with frequencies above 20 kHz) are sent into the metal. If there is a crack or hole, the waves reflect from that point. These reflected waves are captured by a detector, and their analysis helps identify the defect. This is a crucial part of Non-Destructive Testing (NDT), widely used in industrial inspections.

Extra Facts:
1. Ultrasonic waves are also used in ultrasonography in the medical field to create images of internal organs.
2. The technique employs piezoelectric crystals, which convert electrical signals into mechanical waves and vice versa.
3. Ultrasonic Testing is applied in pipelines, aircraft, and bridges to detect structural flaws without damaging the material.

question:

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: sound energy into electrical energy
sound energy into mechanical energy
mechanical energy into sound energy
electrical energy into sound energy
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is sound energy into electrical energy

Explanation:
A microphone is a transducer that converts sound energy into electrical energy. It transforms pressure waves (mechanical waves) of sound into electrical signals. It consists of a diaphragm that vibrates due to sound waves, and these vibrations are converted into electrical signals using a coil or capacitor. This process is called electromechanical transduction. Microphones are used in communication, recording, and sound amplification.

question:
What is the speed of sound in air?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: 343 m/s
373 m/s
434 m/s
383 m/s
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 343 m/s

Explanation:
The speed of sound in air is 343 meters per second (m/s) at a temperature of 20°C. The speed of sound depends on the density and temperature of the medium. As temperature increases, the speed of sound increases because the kinetic energy of the molecules increases. Sound is a mechanical wave that requires a medium for propagation. It is expressed by the equation v = √(γRT/M), where v is the speed of sound, γ is the ratio of specific heats, R is the gas constant, T is the temperature in Kelvin, and M is the molar mass.

Extra Facts:
The speed of sound varies in different media. In water, it is 1482 m/s, and in steel, it is approximately 5960 m/s. Sound cannot travel in a vacuum because there is no medium. The Mach number represents the speed of an object relative to the speed of sound. Sound waves are longitudinal waves, where the particles of the medium vibrate in the direction of the wave.

☛ What happens to the speed of sound when temperature increases? → It increases
☛ What does the Mach number represent? → Speed of an object relative to the speed of sound

Extra Facts:
ध्वनि की गति विभिन्न माध्यमों में अलग-अलग होती है। जल में यह 1482 m/s और स्टील में लगभग 5960 m/s होती है। ध्वनि निर्वात में नहीं चल सकती क्योंकि वहां कोई माध्यम नहीं होता। मैक संख्या ध्वनि की गति के सापेक्ष किसी वस्तु की गति को दर्शाती है। ध्वनि तरंगें अनुदैर्ध्य तरंगें होती हैं, जिनमें माध्यम के कण तरंग की दिशा में ही कंपन करते हैं।

question:
What is the lowest frequency of sound that can be heard by human beings?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: 50 Hz
500 Hz
20 Hz
10 Hz
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 20 Hz

Explanation:
The lowest frequency of sound that can be heard by human beings is 20 Hz. Sound frequency is measured in Hertz (Hz). The human ear can typically hear frequencies ranging from 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz. This range is known as the Audible Range. Sounds with frequencies below 20 Hz are called Infrasonic Sound, while sounds with frequencies above 20,000 Hz are called Ultrasonic Sound. Both types of sounds cannot be heard by the human ear.

Extra Facts:
Sound waves are mechanical waves that require a medium (such as air, water, or solids) for propagation. The speed of sound depends on the density and elasticity of the medium. In air, the speed of sound is approximately 343 m/s. Sound waves are used in various fields, including medicine (ultrasound), communication (radio, telephone), and industries. Animals like dolphins and bats use ultrasonic sound for echolocation.

solution:

Explanation:
The speed of sound in a medium depends on the density and elasticity of that medium. In solids, the speed of sound is the highest because the molecules are closely packed, allowing sound waves to travel faster.

At 25°C, the speed of sound in the given options is:

- Steel: ~5960 m/s
- Iron: ~5130 m/s
- Aluminium: ~6420 m/s

Aluminium has the highest speed of sound because it has a high Young's Modulus and low density, enabling sound waves to propagate faster.

Extra Facts:
- The speed of sound varies in different media: Solid > Liquid > Gas
- In air, the speed of sound is ~343 m/s (at 25°C), while in water, it is ~1482 m/s.
- The speed of sound depends on temperature, pressure, and the properties of the medium.
- Diamond has the highest speed of sound (~12,000 m/s) because it is the hardest material.

question:
The SONAR technique is used to determine the:

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: air distance
depth of the sea
land surface distance
height of a mountain
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is depth of the sea

Explanation:
SONAR (Sound Navigation and Ranging) is a technique used to measure the distance, direction, and depth of objects underwater. It works on the principle of sound waves. The SONAR device emits sound waves (usually ultrasonic) that travel through water, and when these waves hit an object and return as echoes, the distance and depth are calculated based on the time taken. This technology is useful for measuring sea depth, detecting submarines, and creating marine maps. The depth is determined using the speed of sound waves and the echo return time.

Extra Facts:
SONAR technology was developed during World War I to detect submarines. It is widely used in oceanography, fishing, and military applications. There are two types of SONAR: active SONAR (emits sound waves) and passive SONAR (only listens to sound waves). Sound waves travel in water at approximately 1500 meters per second.

question:
What is the velocity of sound in air ?

[SSC CGL 2019]
options: 220 m/sec
232 m/sec
343 m/sec
110 m/sec
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 343 m/sec

Explanation:
The velocity of sound in air is 343 meters per second (m/s) at a temperature of 20°C. The speed of sound depends on the density and elasticity of the medium. In air, the speed of sound changes with temperature because as temperature increases, the kinetic energy of air molecules increases, allowing sound waves to travel faster. The speed of sound is given by the formula v = 331 + (0.6 × T), where T is the temperature in Celsius. At 20°C, it becomes 331 + (0.6 × 20) = 343 m/s.

Extra Facts:
The speed of sound varies in different media. For example, it is 1482 m/s in water and 5960 m/s in steel. Sound cannot travel in a vacuum because it requires a medium (such as air, water, or solid) to propagate. The first scientist to measure the speed of sound was Pierre Gassendi, who studied it in the 17th century.

हवा में ध्वनि का वेग 343 मीटर प्रति सेकंड (m/s) होता है, जब हवा का तापमान 20°C होता है। ध्वनि का वेग माध्यम के घनत्व और लोच पर निर्भर करता है। हवा में ध्वनि का वेग तापमान के साथ बदलता है, क्योंकि तापमान बढ़ने से हवा के अणुओं की गतिज ऊर्जा बढ़ती है, जिससे ध्वनि तरंगें तेजी से यात्रा करती हैं। ध्वनि का वेग सूत्र v = 331 + (0.6 × T) द्वारा दिया जाता है, जहां T सेल्सियस में तापमान है। 20°C पर, यह 331 + (0.6 × 20) = 343 m/s होता है।

Extra Facts:
ध्वनि का वेग विभिन्न माध्यमों में अलग-अलग होता है। जैसे, पानी में यह 1482 m/s और स्टील में 5960 m/s होता है। ध्वनि निर्वात में यात्रा नहीं कर सकती क्योंकि इसके लिए एक माध्यम (जैसे हवा, पानी, ठोस) की आवश्यकता होती है। ध्वनि की गति को मापने वाले पहले वैज्ञानिक पियरे गैसेंडी थे, जिन्होंने 17वीं शताब्दी में इसका अध्ययन किया था।

question:
The technology that uses the reflection of ultrasound waves to produce images of the heart is known as :

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: echocardiogram
echocardiography
ultrasonography
sonography
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is echocardiography

Explanation:
Echocardiography is a medical imaging technique that uses ultrasound waves to produce images of the heart's structure and function. This technology works on the principle of Doppler effect and echo reflection. The ultrasound waves bounce off the heart tissues and return to the transducer, which captures them and converts them into images via a computer. It helps diagnose heart conditions such as valvular heart disease, myocardial issues, and congenital heart defects.

Extra Facts:
Echocardiography is of two types: Transthoracic Echocardiography (TTE) and Transesophageal Echocardiography (TEE). In TTE, the transducer is placed on the chest, while in TEE, it is inserted into the esophagus. This technique is non-invasive and painless, making it safe for patients. The frequency of ultrasound waves typically ranges from 2-18 MHz, which is beyond the human audible range (20 Hz-20 kHz).

दिल की छवियों को बनाने के लिए अल्ट्रासाउंड तरंगों के प्रतिबिंब का उपयोग करने वाली तकनीक को कहा जाता है

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options_hi: इकोकार्डियोग्राम
इकोकार्डियोग्राफी
अल्ट्रासोनोग्राफी
सोनोग्राफ़ी
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है इकोकार्डियोग्राफी

Explanation:
इकोकार्डियोग्राफी एक मेडिकल इमेजिंग तकनीक है जो अल्ट्रासाउंड तरंगों का उपयोग करके हृदय की संरचना और कार्यप्रणाली की छवियां बनाती है। यह तकनीक डॉपलर इफेक्ट और प्रतिध्वनि (echo) के सिद्धांत पर काम करती है। अल्ट्रासाउंड तरंगें हृदय के ऊतकों से टकराकर वापस लौटती हैं, जिन्हें एक ट्रांसड्यूसर द्वारा पकड़ा जाता है और कंप्यूटर द्वारा छवियों में परिवर्तित किया जाता है। यह हृदय रोगों जैसे वाल्वुलर हृदय रोग, हृदय की मांसपेशियों की समस्याओं और जन्मजात हृदय दोषों का निदान करने में मदद करता है।

Extra Facts:
इकोकार्डियोग्राफी दो प्रकार की होती है: ट्रांसथोरैसिक इकोकार्डियोग्राफी (TTE) और ट्रांसइसोफेजियल इकोकार्डियोग्राफी (TEE)। TTE में ट्रांसड्यूसर को छाती पर रखा जाता है, जबकि TEE में इसे अन्नप्रणाली में डाला जाता है। यह तकनीक गैर-आक्रामक और दर्द रहित है, जिससे यह रोगियों के लिए सुरक्षित है। अल्ट्रासाउंड तरंगों की आवृत्ति आमतौर पर 2-18 MHz होती है, जो मानव श्रव्य सीमा (20 Hz-20 kHz) से अधिक होती है।
